name: Jordan
summary_text: Jordan demands real caution from trans visitors — the safest of the Levantine Arab states by a clear margin, but on a deteriorating trajectory. Same-sex intimacy was decriminalised in 1951, and courts have granted legal gender recognition in individual cases (the 2014 Court of Cassation ruling — though justified by reclassifying the plaintiff as intersex). There is no statute criminalising gender expression itself. The deterioration is documented: Cairo 52 reports a notable rise in targeting of transgender individuals and spaces by both security forces and civilians, using Ottoman/British-era morality laws; Jordanian security forces coerced queer community spaces into complete cessation of activities; the 2023 cybercrime law (“inciting immorality”) gives authorities a digital tool against LGBT expression; and gender-affirming surgery is criminalised for trans people (Article 8, Medical and Health Liability Law) while permitted for intersex people. In 2021 security forces arrested 14 people at a private party. For a visitor: no legal exposure for gender expression per se, but morality-law discretion, shuttered community infrastructure, and family-society hostility make outing dangerous.

sources.title: Jordan | Cairo 52 Legal Research Institute
sources.claim_summary: Cairo 52 country review of Jordan: notable rise in targeting of trans individuals and spaces by law enforcement and civilians, using Ottoman/British-mandate-era morality laws; new legislation curtails LGBTQ+ speech and digital access; security forces coerced queer community spaces to cease activities, prompting many trans people to leave; legal gender recognition and gender-affirming healthcare are prohibited (intersex people can change markers); medical-liability law penalises professionals providing transition care.

sources.title: Jordan | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International country overview (updated March 2026): same-sex intimacy decriminalised in 1951; honour killings criminalised 2013; some trans people have changed markers but no clear legal pathway; Article 8 of the 2018 Medical and Health Liability Law criminalises gender-affirming surgery for trans people (allowed for intersex); the 2023 Cybercrime Law criminalises online 'promotion of immorality'; public-decency laws enable arbitrary arrests and event shutdowns.

sources.title: Jordan: New Threats to Civic Space | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: Human Rights Watch (Jan 2024): 'Jordan: New Threats to Civic Space' — shrinking freedoms of expression and association, affecting LGBT Jordanians among others.

sources.title: Case No 2092/2014 – Jordan | Cairo 52 Legal Research Institute
sources.claim_summary: Cairo 52 case digest, Jordanian Court of Cassation Case No 2092/2014 (Oct 2014): granted a young woman's request to amend her documents to reflect her gender change - but justified it by finding she was intersex, not transgender; Jordanian law criminalises sex reassignment (up to 10 years) except for intersex people; the plaintiff had undergone transition procedures overseas for her safety.

sources.title: Beyond Decriminalization of Same-Sex Relations | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: Human Rights Watch (Jun 2024): 'Beyond Decriminalization of Same-Sex Relations' — what states must do once sodomy laws are gone, in the regional context of Jordan.

HRW report (April 2018) 'Audacity in Adversity': LGBT activism in the Middle East and North Africa - despite state-sponsored repression and stigma, LGBT people are speaking out, building alliances and regional movements; includes an annex of laws used to punish same-sex conduct and gender expression across MENA (Jordan among them).

sources.title: SogiNews
sources.claim_summary: SogiNews (archived RFSL 'LGBT Voices' project, Sida-funded): MENA section of the archived SOGI news site - legacy coverage of sexual-orientation and gender-identity news in the Middle East and North Africa region.

sources.title: Jordan: Security Forces Target LGBT Activists | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: HRW (Dec 2023): 'Jordan: Security Forces Target LGBT Activists' - documents Jordanian security forces' harassment and targeting of LGBT activists, despite Jordan not criminalising same-sex conduct.
